title: Music’s ‘Bonanza Year’ for Funding and More Insights from GoldState’s Conversations in Music Conference
summary: Key topics included the merging of independent companies and the financial prospects for rights holders as streaming revenues soar.
body: Earlier this month, GoldState Music founder and managing partner Charles Goldstuck held a three-day conference about the newsiest topics in the music business and among others, he shared this takeaway: “We should expect 2027 to be a bonanza year for investment activity.” A major-label executive, Goldstuck co-founded J Records with Clive Davis , later building it into the RCA Music Group, served as BMG’s president and chief operating officer, led TouchTunes’s shift toward connected, interactive digital jukeboxes and founded HitCo Entertainment with L.A. Reid. More recently, he has led GoldState Music’s investments in the catalogs of artists like Alan Walker and companies like indie audiobook platform Podium and distributor Too Lost and authored an academic paper on how the music industry can adopt and monetize AI music. Since he founded a state-of-the-art recording studio and music academy in the Bahamas called  The Sanctuary at Albany in 2018, GoldState has had a unique vantage point into the broadening commitment to invest in music.
